easy.explanation: Ecclesiastes 11:1 says, “Cast thy bread upon the waters.”
easy.q: What does the verse say to cast upon the waters?

easy.explanation: The verse says, “Give a portion to seven, and also to eight.”
easy.q: To how many should a person give a portion?

easy.explanation: The verse promises, “thou shalt find it after many days,” referring to the bread cast upon the waters.
easy.q: What may a person find after many days?

medium.explanation: The instruction suggests spreading resources rather than depending on only one possibility.
medium.q: What does giving to seven and also to eight suggest?

answers: Because he does not know what evil may come upon the earth
Because every choice is guaranteed to succeed
medium.explanation: The reason given is, “thou knowest not what evil shall be upon the earth.”
medium.q: Why should a person give to several rather than only one?

answers: Generosity always brings an immediate reward
medium.explanation: The wording points to a delayed or later result rather than an immediate one.
medium.q: What is implied by finding the bread after many days?

answers: Act generously while also spreading risk
Wait until the outcome is certain
challenge.explanation: The passage joins generosity with careful distribution because the future is uncertain.
challenge.q: What practical principle combines the two verses?

challenge.explanation: The phrase reminds the reader that people cannot know what trouble may arise.
challenge.q: What does the phrase “thou knowest not” emphasize?

answers: One loss may not destroy everything
It removes the need to act
challenge.explanation: Spreading resources can limit the harm caused by an unexpected misfortune.
challenge.q: Why is distributing portions a wise response to possible evil?

paragraphs.title: Uncertainty and the Need to Act

answers: They empty themselves upon the earth
easy.explanation: Ecclesiastes 11:3 says that full clouds empty themselves upon the earth.
The verse says, “He that observeth the wind shall not sow.”
easy.q: What will the person who observes the wind not do?

easy.explanation: The instruction is, “In the morning sow thy seed.”
easy.q: What should a person do in the morning?

answers: Do not stop working or trying
Do not sow in the morning
medium.explanation: The phrase encourages continued effort, especially in the evening.
medium.q: What does “withhold not thine hand” mean in context?

answers: He may never sow or reap
medium.explanation: The verses warn that watching the wind and clouds can prevent a person from acting.
medium.q: What may happen to someone who waits for perfect conditions?

medium.explanation: The passage says no one knows whether one effort, the other, or both will prosper.
medium.q: Why does the passage mention not knowing which effort will prosper?

answers: People should act despite incomplete understanding
People should wait for a complete explanation
challenge.explanation: Human uncertainty is presented as a reason to act faithfully, not as a reason to become inactive.
challenge.q: What conclusion follows from not knowing the works of God?

answers: Because no one knows which effort will succeed
Because morning and evening are identical
challenge.explanation: The verse encourages repeated effort because the result of either attempt is unknown.
challenge.q: Why does the writer recommend sowing both in the morning and in the evening?

challenge.explanation: The passage contrasts watching conditions indefinitely with sowing and continuing to work.
challenge.q: What central contrast appears in this passage?

easy.explanation: Ecclesiastes 11:7 says, “Truly the light is sweet.”
The verse calls it pleasant for the eyes to behold the sun.
easy.q: What is pleasant for the eyes to behold?

easy.explanation: The passage says that if a person lives many years, he should rejoice in them all.
easy.q: What should a person do during all his years?

medium.explanation: Here, “vanity” emphasizes that earthly life and experiences do not last forever.
medium.q: What does “vanity” mean in this context?

answers: To remember that life is temporary
To forget the years of life
medium.explanation: Remembering darkness gives perspective on the temporary nature of life.
medium.q: Why should a person remember the days of darkness?

answers: Enjoying the light while remembering darkness
medium.explanation: The verses encourage joy in life while also remembering difficult and limited days.
medium.q: What balance does the passage present?

answers: Enjoyment should be aware of life’s brevity
challenge.explanation: The contrast teaches that life is good to enjoy but is not endless.
challenge.q: What does the movement from light to darkness teach?

answers: They represent present enjoyment and future limitation
They prove that people control the future
challenge.explanation: The sun portrays the goodness of life, while darkness reminds the reader of hardship and mortality.
challenge.q: How do the sun and the days of darkness function together?

answers: He might fail to enjoy the light and life
He would understand everything about the future
challenge.explanation: The passage calls for a balanced response rather than a rejection of joy.
challenge.q: What could happen if someone remembered only the days of darkness?

paragraphs.title: The Joy of Youth and Responsibility for Choice

easy.explanation: The verse addresses the “young man” and tells him to rejoice in his youth.
easy.q: To whom does the command “Rejoice” address itself?

answers: In the ways of his heart and in the sight of his eyes
Only in the ways of other people
easy.explanation: The verse mentions the ways of the heart and the sight of the eyes.
easy.q: Where may the young man walk?

easy.explanation: The verse says, “for all these things God will bring thee into judgment.”
easy.q: What will God bring upon the young man for all these things?

answers: Hide sorrow from other people only
medium.explanation: The instruction is to remove sorrow or distress from the heart.
medium.q: What does “remove sorrow from thy heart” mean?

answers: Joy is permitted, but choices remain accountable
Judgment removes every possibility of joy
A joyful person has no responsibility
medium.explanation: The passage allows rejoicing but immediately reminds the young person of judgment.
medium.q: How are youthful joy and judgment connected?

answers: The young person should reject harmful conduct
The young person should seek more trouble
The young person should remember only the sun
medium.explanation: The verse pairs removing sorrow with putting away evil.
medium.q: What does the command to put away evil from the flesh indicate?

challenge.explanation: The young person may follow his desires, yet God will judge all these choices.
challenge.q: What is the main tension in these verses?

answers: Personal freedom should be joined with awareness of consequences
challenge.explanation: The command to enjoy life is balanced by the command to remember future judgment.
challenge.q: What does “walk in the ways of thine heart” together with “know thou” imply?

answers: It reminds the young person that youth and its pleasures pass away
It forbids every form of joy
challenge.explanation: The word “vanity” emphasizes the temporary nature of childhood, youth, and their pleasures.
challenge.q: How does “childhood and youth are vanity” affect the instruction to rejoice?
